stories.headline: Alibaba Revealed Behind HappyHorse-1.0, Top-Ranked AI Video Generation Model

key_facts.fact: Alibaba confirmed it created HappyHorse-1.0, an anonymous AI video model that topped blind-test rankings on Artificial Analysis for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation.
The model was developed by Alibaba's ATH AI Innovation Unit and is still under development; the developers revealed the connection Friday via a newly created X account.
Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares closed 2.12% higher Friday after the reveal, following a 6.75% rise Wednesday amid speculation about the model's origin.
The reveal comes as OpenAI recently discontinued its Sora video generation app and ByteDance paused Seedance 2.0 over copyright disputes with Hollywood studios.

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Splashes Down in Pacific After Historic 10-Day Moon Flyby Mission

key_facts.fact: NASA's Orion capsule 'Integrity' splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego at 8:07 PM EDT on April 10, ending the 10-day Artemis II mission — the first crewed voyage beyond low Earth orbit in over 53 years
All four crew members — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — were recovered safely and reported healthy
The crew set a new human spaceflight distance record of 252,756 miles from Earth during the lunar flyby, surpassing Apollo 13's record by more than 4,100 miles

The capsule re-entered at nearly Mach 33 (about 24,661 mph), enduring temperatures above 5,000°F on its heat shield — the first crewed test of Orion's heat shield, which had known design flaws from an unmanned 2022 flight

Glover became the first Black astronaut, Koch the first woman, and Hansen the first non-American to fly to the Moon; the mission paves the way for Artemis III (2027) and a lunar landing on Artemis IV (2028)

stories.headline: Blackstone Files for ~$2B Data Center REIT IPO Targeting AI Hyperscaler Facilities

key_facts.fact: Blackstone filed for an IPO of Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Inc. (ticker BXDC) on Friday, a new data-center acquisition vehicle that plans to buy already-built and leased properties.

The vehicle will target newly built data centers valued at $250M to $1.5B each, leased to investment-grade hyperscalers, with expected yields of 5.75%–7%+ per year and automatic rent escalators of 2–3% annually.
Bloomberg reported Blackstone plans to raise approximately $2 billion, with Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley as joint lead book-running managers.

The REIT is currently a 'blind pool' with no acquired assets yet. It will be externally managed by BX REIT, an affiliate of Blackstone, which manages $77B in infrastructure capital and $319B in real estate investor capital.
Blackstone estimates the total addressable stabilized data center market at approximately $1 trillion over the next five years.

stories.headline: China to Ban Sulphuric Acid Exports From May as Hormuz Blockade Cuts Global Sulphur Supply

key_facts.fact: China has notified producers it will halt sulphuric acid exports from May, hitting metals and fertilizer industries already strained by Hormuz-related raw material shortages; the ban could last throughout 2026

The Middle East produces one-third of the world's sulphur, a raw material for sulphuric acid used in copper extraction and phosphate fertilizers; the Strait of Hormuz blockade has cut off these shipments
Chile — the world's No. 1 copper producer — buys over 1 million tonnes of Chinese sulphuric acid annually; about one-fifth of Chilean copper output depends on sulphuric acid processing
China's move comes during peak crop-planting season and will further pressure copper-mining industries in Chile, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Zambia

stories.headline: Canada's Cohere and Germany's Aleph Alpha in Advanced Merger Talks With Berlin's Backing

key_facts.fact: AI companies Cohere (Canada) and Aleph Alpha (Germany) are in advanced merger talks that started early this year, with plans for the new entity to be headquartered in both countries.
The German government would be willing to become a key customer of a combined company, as part of a push to provide digital public services.
German Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger called a potential deal a 'very strong signal,' saying Germany and Canada were already collaborating closely in AI.
Aleph Alpha told Reuters that strategic partnership discussions were standard practice and that it had its own independent strategy, declining to comment further.

stories.headline: CoreWeave Lands Multi-Year Cloud Deal With Anthropic; Shares Surge Over 13%

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave struck a multi-year agreement with Anthropic to supply cloud computing capacity for Claude AI model workloads, with financial terms undisclosed.
CoreWeave shares surged more than 13% on Friday following the announcement, trading at $102.73.
CoreWeave now serves nine of the ten major developers of large language models, having previously signed an $11.9B deal with OpenAI and an expanded $21B deal with Meta.
The deal helps CoreWeave diversify revenue beyond Microsoft, which accounted for about 67% of its revenue last year.
Anthropic has been rushing to secure more capacity, having also signed a deal with Broadcom and Google for AI capacity and exploring its own chip design.

stories.headline: CoreWeave Signs Multiyear Deal With Anthropic, Now Serves 9 of Top 10 AI Labs

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave announced a multiyear agreement with Anthropic to provide data center capacity using various Nvidia chip architectures at its US data centers for Claude AI model workloads.
CoreWeave now serves 9 of the 10 major developers of large language models, according to CEO Michael Intrator, with clients including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Meta.
CoreWeave shares surged more than 12% on Friday to $102.73 following the announcement.
CoreWeave currently operates 43 active data centers and has contracted more than 3 gigawatts of server farm power capacity.
The deal follows CoreWeave's recent $8.5 billion capital raise led by Meta and Meta's $21 billion compute commitment to CoreWeave.
Anthropic has pledged $50 billion for new AI data centers in the US and earlier this week partnered with Broadcom and Google to secure 3.5 GW of energy.

stories.headline: FDA Rejects Replimune's Melanoma Drug RP1 for the Second Time, Triggering Job Cuts

key_facts.fact: The FDA on April 10 issued a second Complete Response Letter rejecting Replimune's RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) for advanced melanoma, saying the data are 'insufficient to conclude substantial evidence of effectiveness'
In the IGNYTE trial, RP1 plus nivolumab showed a 34% response rate with a median duration of 24.8 months in patients whose melanoma progressed on anti-PD-1 therapy

A senior member of the prior FDA review team had publicly stated 'the BLA clinical team thought the applicant had provided adequate evidence' but leadership disagreed; a different review team was assigned for the resubmission

Replimune announced it will eliminate jobs and substantially scale back US manufacturing; CEO Sushil Patel said the treatment 'will not be available — not because the medicine failed, because the system did'
Replimune shares fell about 20% on the news; the case has become a flashpoint in the debate over FDA review standards under Vinay Prasad's leadership of the biologics division

stories.headline: METR and Epoch AI Show AI Agents Can Autonomously Complete Weeks-Long Coding Tasks

key_facts.fact: MirrorCode is a benchmark co-developed by METR and Epoch AI of long-horizon coding tasks derived from real software applications, testing AI ability to reimplement CLI programs without access to source code.
Claude Opus 4.6 successfully reimplemented gotree, a bioinformatics toolkit with ~16,000 lines of Go and 40+ commands, a task estimated to take a human engineer 2–17 weeks without AI assistance.
The benchmark includes more than 20 target programs spanning Unix utilities, data serialization, bioinformatics, interpreters, static analysis, cryptography, and compression.
The researchers observed continued gains from inference scaling on larger projects, suggesting bigger tasks may be solvable given enough tokens.
AI agents are given execute-only access to the original program and visible test cases but no source code, requiring them to make architectural design decisions autonomously.

stories.headline: OpenAI Pauses Stargate UK Data Center Project Over Energy Costs and Regulation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has paused its Stargate UK data center project in north-east England, citing rising energy costs and regulatory uncertainty as key barriers.

The project was part of a wider £31 billion UK tech investment package announced in September 2025, in partnership with Nvidia and Nscale, with plans to deploy up to 8,000 GPUs in Q1 2026 scaling to 31,000.
OpenAI said it would only move forward 'when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment,' citing copyright rules as a specific concern.
The UK government recently withdrew proposals that would have permitted AI developers to use copyrighted material unless rights holders opted out, drawing tech sector criticism.
OpenAI also decided not to lease an expansion to its Abilene, Texas Stargate site; the pause comes as the company reins in spending ahead of a planned public listing.

stories.headline: Three OpenAI Stargate Infrastructure Leaders Leave to Join Meta

key_facts.fact: Peter Hoeschele, who played a critical role in OpenAI's Stargate initiative and led work on the Abilene, Texas data center site, is joining Meta along with Shamez Hemani (computing strategy and business development) and Anuj Saharan (computing organization leader).
Meta CEO Zuckerberg has pledged up to $135 billion in capital expenditures for 2026 alone, focused on AI infrastructure, with plans to spend hundreds of billions more by the end of the decade.
OpenAI previously said it was grateful for the three employees' contributions and hired former Intel Corp. executive Sachin Katti in November to lead its industrial compute efforts.

Stargate was announced last year at the White House as a $500 billion venture between OpenAI, Oracle, and SoftBank. OpenAI also paused its Stargate UK project and decided not to lease an expansion to the Abilene, Texas site.

stories.headline: Ramp Data: Anthropic's US Business Adoption Jumps to 30.6%, Closing Gap With OpenAI

key_facts.fact: 30.6% of US businesses paid for Anthropic's tools in March, up from 24.4% in February — a 6.2 percentage point jump in one month.
OpenAI's US business adoption remained nearly flat month-over-month at approximately 35%.
Anthropic went from capturing roughly 10% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic business subscription spend in early 2025 to commanding over 65% by February 2026.
Sectors with the deepest AI adoption — Information, Finance, Professional Services — show the widest Anthropic lead over OpenAI.
The divergence is driven by strong interest in Claude Code products; Anthropic's annualized revenue surpassed $30 billion, with 80% from business customers.

stories.headline: Tesla FSD Supervised Gets First European Approval in the Netherlands

key_facts.fact: The Dutch vehicle authority RDW granted type approval for Tesla's FSD Supervised on April 10, making the Netherlands the first European market to authorize the system on public roads.

The approval followed more than 18 months of testing on both the RDW's own test track and Dutch public roads. FSD Supervised complies with UN R-171 standards and benefits from Article 39 exemptions under EU Regulation 2018/858.

The driver remains fully responsible and must maintain attention at all times; the RDW approved FSD as an advanced driver assistance system, not autonomous technology. Drivers don't need hands on the wheel but sensors monitor alertness.
About 100,000 Tesla Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in the Netherlands are eligible for the FSD software. Tesla is the most popular EV maker in the Netherlands.
The RDW will submit an application for EU-wide approval to the European Commission. All 27 member states will vote; Tesla anticipates possible EU-wide recognition during summer 2026.

Elon Musk commented: 'First (supervised) FSD approval in Europe! Congratulations to the Tesla team and thank you to the regulatory authorities in the Netherlands for all the hard work required to make this happen.'

stories.headline: US March CPI Surges to 3.3% as Iran War Energy Shock Drives Biggest Monthly Spike in 4 Years

key_facts.fact: US CPI rose 0.9% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year in March, the largest annual increase since May 2024 and biggest monthly jump in nearly four years
Energy prices surged 10.9% in March, with gasoline jumping 21.2% — the largest single-month gasoline increase on record — accounting for nearly three-quarters of the overall monthly CPI increase
Core CPI (excluding food and energy) rose a modest 0.2% month-on-month and 2.6% year-on-year, suggesting the inflation spike is energy-driven rather than broad-based
University of Michigan consumer sentiment plunged to 47.6 in April from 53.3 in March — the lowest level since the survey began in 1952; 12-month inflation expectations surged to 4.8% from 3.8%
Gasoline prices averaged $4.15/gallon nationally, up roughly 40% from $2.98 before the Iran war began, according to AAA

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said oil shock extends the timeline for getting inflation to 2%, and the Fed may hold rates steady; she placed lower probability on a rate hike than on a cut or hold

stories.headline: Vance Arrives in Islamabad for Iran Peace Talks as Tehran Sets Preconditions and Trump Threatens War

key_facts.fact: VP JD Vance departed for Islamabad on April 10 with envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for Pakistan-mediated peace talks with Iran, telling reporters 'We're looking forward to the negotiation. I think it's going to be positive'

Iran's parliamentary speaker Ghalibaf posted that 'a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of Iran's blocked assets' must be fulfilled before negotiations can begin; his delegation arrived in Islamabad with security, political, military, economic, and legal teams
Trump told the New York Post the US is 'loading up the ships with the best weapons ever made' during the ceasefire pause, warning 'if we don't have a deal, we will be using them'
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively blocked with 68+ loaded tankers trapped in the Persian Gulf; only about 22 ships have passed since the ceasefire on April 7, versus 100+ per day pre-war

Israel and Lebanon will hold direct negotiations starting Tuesday in Washington; more than 300 people were killed in Israeli strikes on Beirut the day the Iran ceasefire was announced, and at least 1,953 have died in Lebanon total
More than 3,000 people have been killed in Iran and 13 US service members have died since the war began roughly six weeks ago

stories.headline: Xi Jinping Meets Taiwan's KMT Leader in Beijing — First Such Talks in a Decade

key_facts.fact: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun at Beijing's Great Hall of the People on April 10 — the first official meeting between sitting CCP and KMT leaders since November 2016
Xi said 'we need peace, we need development, we need communication and we need cooperation' and declared he 'absolutely would not tolerate' Taiwan independence
The meeting comes weeks before a planned May summit between Xi and Trump in Beijing, where Taiwan is expected to be high on the agenda alongside U.S. arms sales to the island
Taiwan's defense ministry detected 16 Chinese warplanes flying near the island during the same hours Xi and Cheng were meeting on Friday morning
Cheng's KMT has been blocking a stalled $40 billion defense spending bill in Taiwan's parliament; an April poll showed the KMT commands less than a third of popular support

stories.headline: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Shot Down Iranian Drones in Multiple Gulf States, Signs 10-Year Deals

key_facts.fact: Zelensky revealed on April 10 that Ukrainian military experts successfully shot down Iranian Shahed-type drones 'in several countries' in the Middle East using domestically produced interceptor drones and electronic warfare systems
Ukraine sent more than 200 experts to the Middle East and signed 10-year security agreements with Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar; talks are underway with Oman, Kuwait, and Bahrain
In exchange for drone defense expertise, Ukraine receives Patriot PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors for its own air defense, along with oil and diesel supplies and financial agreements
Zelensky described the deployment as 'not about a training mission or exercises, but about support in building a modern air defence system that can actually work'
Zelensky also confirmed Ukraine's military will participate in consultations on the future operation of the Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: China's Zhiyuan Robot Spins Off Quadruped Unit, Targets ¥500M Revenue in 2026

key_facts.fact: Zhiyuan Robot (智元机器人, also known as Agibot) spun off its quadruped robot business into a new independent subsidiary called Zhiyuan Kutuo (智元酷拓).
Zhiyuan Kutuo targets ¥500M in revenue for 2026. By 2030, the company plans to ship 300,000 units per year and reach ¥10B in annual revenue, with overseas revenue exceeding 35%.

IDC forecasts China's quadruped robot market will exceed $700 million in 2026, doubling year-over-year. Zhiyuan Kutuo projects the broader ecosystem (including upstream, hardware add-ons, software, and services) will reach ¥100 billion by 2030.

The product line spans logistics, industrial inspection, security patrol, firefighting, and education. The next-gen flagship D2 Max is positioned as the industry's first L3-level all-terrain autonomous quadruped robot.
Unitree leads the global quadruped market with 32.4% sales share, followed by DeepRobotics at 18.9%, according to IDC data for 2024. Q1 2026 overseas orders for Zhiyuan Kutuo already reached 40%.
